tagline: A UNESCO colonial harbor where ~50 schooners already sail every day, a tropical fjord hides around the headland, and the prettiest beaches can only be reached by boat.
summary: Paraty is the western anchor of Rio state's Costa Verde — a 17th-century gold-route port whose cobbled historic center still floods gently with the tide, inscribed by UNESCO in 2019 as Brazil's first mixed (culture + biodiversity) World Heritage site together with Ilha Grande. The town's mobility pattern is already water-first: a fleet of roughly 50 tour schooners plus dozens of lanchas departs the Cais de Turismo daily for the bay's ~65 islands, the Saco do Mamanguá fjord and beaches like Praia da Lula, while caiçara fishing villages such as Praia do Sono and Ponta Negra are reachable only by trail or open taxi-boat. Foiling-electric vessels fly silent and zero-wake through these protected Atlantic-forest waters, collapse the slow schooner-and-lancha transfers, and knit Paraty to Ilha Grande and Angra dos Reis into one clean UNESCO water corridor.

demand_signals.label: Visitor volume
demand_signals.value: ~3.5 million tourists and visitors per year (municipal estimate)
demand_signals.note: Tourism represents ~80% of the local economy in a town of ~45,000 residents
demand_signals.source: Prefeitura de Paraty (Mayor Luciano Vidal) via Diário do Vale; Valor Econômico (Jul 2026)

demand_signals.label: Tour-boat fleet
demand_signals.value: ~50 schooners based in Paraty, average capacity ~150 passengers, sailing daily bay circuits at R$60–100 per person
demand_signals.note: An adopted daily boarding habit at the Cais de Turismo — the demand is already on the water, on slow diesel hulls
demand_signals.source: Associação das Escunas de Paraty via Valor Econômico (Feb 2026)

demand_signals.label: UNESCO twin site
demand_signals.value: "Paraty and Ilha Grande — Culture and Biodiversity" inscribed 2019: Brazil's first mixed World Heritage site
demand_signals.note: The two halves of the inscription sit ~31 nm apart across the Baía da Ilha Grande — a natural heritage water corridor

demand_signals.label: Event surge
demand_signals.value: FLIP literary festival drew ~34,000 attendees over 5 days in 2025 (+10% year on year), saturating a 45,000-resident town
demand_signals.note: Repeated surge windows (FLIP in July, Festival da Cachaça, Carnival) overwhelm road access and hotel capacity

demand_signals.label: Marina infrastructure
demand_signals.value: Marina Porto Imperial holds ~200 covered dry berths + 150 wet berths minutes from the historic center, alongside Marina do Engenho
demand_signals.note: A ready berthing and shore-power backbone for an electric fleet

demand_signals.label: Boat-only access
demand_signals.value: Praia do Sono, Antigos and Ponta Negra — among Brazil's most celebrated wild beaches — are reachable only by trail or open taxi-boat (R$40–60 per leg from Laranjeiras)
demand_signals.note: Whole communities and beach economies already depend on small-boat links
demand_signals.source: Grupo Dicas travel guide (2026); local taxi-boat operators

use_cases.title: Modernize the schooner habit
use_cases.body: Tens of thousands of visitors already board boats at the Cais de Turismo every week for the Ilha dos Cocos–Lagoa Azul–Praia da Lula circuit. A foiling shuttle runs the same beloved stops in a fraction of the time — smooth, silent and zero-wake over the bay's ~65 islands.

use_cases.title: Fjord and hidden-beach spider
use_cases.body: Private foiling day-charters from the marinas into the Saco do Mamanguá — Brazil's only tropical fjord — and on to Praia Vermelha, Ilha do Algodão and the Juatinga wild coast, gliding past caiçara villages without wake or engine noise.

use_cases.title: Caiçara village access
use_cases.body: Fast, dry, all-weather links where today only open wooden taxi-boats run: Laranjeiras to Praia do Sono and Ponta Negra, and the Paraty Mirim spur — community mobility for villages with no road.

use_cases.title: UNESCO twin-site corridor
use_cases.body: Scheduled foiling transfers across the Baía da Ilha Grande linking Paraty's colonial quay with car-free Vila do Abraão (~31 nm) and Angra dos Reis (~28 nm) — one clean water corridor across the whole World Heritage bay, including FLIP surge capacity when the town sells out.

journeys.today: A shared lancha (R$130–300 per person) or a full-day schooner grinds around the headlands into the fjord — most of the day spent in transit.
journeys.with_navier: A ~25-minute silent foiling flight around Ponta Grossa into the 8 km fjord, arriving zero-wake among the caiçara stilt piers.

journeys.today: A van-plus-speedboat combo or a pounding 1.5-hour open lancha (shared transfers from ~R$330 per person; private from ~R$1,890).
journeys.with_navier: A smooth ~75-minute foiling crossing of the Baía da Ilha Grande, linking the two halves of the UNESCO inscription dock-to-dock.

journeys.to: Paraty Mirim / Praia da Lula / Ilha do Algodão
journeys.today: A 100-passenger schooner does the beach circuit in 5–6 hours, anchoring offshore and tendering guests to the sand.
journeys.with_navier: A small-group foiling circuit that reaches the same coves in minutes, close inshore in shallow draft — more stops, no crowds, no wake in the coves.

journeys.today: An open wooden taxi-boat (R$40–60 per leg; ~R$120 round trip to Ponta Negra) that gets wet and choppy on the exposed stretch — or a 1.5-hour forest trail on foot.
journeys.with_navier: A dry, smooth foiling hop above the swell to Brazil's most storied wild beaches and their road-free villages.

journeys.today: A winding 40-minute drive over the serra on the Rio–Santos highway — there is no scheduled boat link to Paraty's most famous surf-and-pools village.
journeys.with_navier: A ~30-minute coastal foiling flight around the headlands, landing off Praia do Meio.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire Paraty mesh sits deep inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope: Cais de Turismo ↔ Paraty Mirim (~5 nm), ↔ Saco do Mamanguá (~7.5 nm), ↔ Trindade (~11 nm), ↔ Laranjeiras/Praia do Sono (~11 nm), with marina charging at Porto Imperial and Engenho. Shallow draft and zero wake matter here: these are protected Atlantic-forest waters, tide-shallow coves and caiçara villages where a conventional boat's wash is felt on every beach.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: For the longer Costa Verde line-hauls — Paraty to Rio de Janeiro's Marina da Glória (~85–90 nm by sea) or onward multi-stop heritage itineraries — Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range runs the corridor with no charging-infrastructure dependency, turning the slow Rio–Santos coastal road into a water route. The Paraty ↔ Ilha Grande (~31 nm) and ↔ Angra (~28 nm) crossings stay all-electric on N35 Shuttle.

competitive_landscape: Paraty's water is worked today by roughly 50 diesel schooners (average ~150 passengers), a large lancha and speedboat charter fleet (Paraty Tours, Rupe Tour, Green Tours and dozens of independents), and caiçara taxi-boats out of Laranjeiras and Paraty Mirim. There is no scheduled public waterway service — every crossing is a tour or a negotiated transfer — and no fast, dry, all-weather option on any corridor. That fleet is the demand evidence: an entire visitor economy already boards boats daily at the Cais de Turismo; the experience is simply slow, loud and diesel in waters UNESCO lists for their biodiversity.
seasonality: December–March (austral summer) is peak: warm water, big crowds, afternoon thunderstorms that scatter the schooner fleet. April–October is a long, drier, calmer shoulder season with mild temperatures — an excellent year-round operating window. Event spikes punctuate the calendar: FLIP in late July (~34,000 attendees), the Festival da Cachaça in August, Carnival and holiday weekends. The inner Baía de Paraty and Mamanguá are well sheltered; the outer Juatinga coast (Trindade, Sono, Ponta Negra) faces open Atlantic swell, where foiling smoothness is the difference between a wet open-boat crossing and a comfortable one. No cyclone exposure.
regulatory_note: The Brazilian Navy (Capitania dos Portos, via the Angra dos Reis delegacia) certifies vessels and crews; ANTAQ regulates waterway passenger services; the Paraty municipality licenses tour operations and manages the Cais de Turismo. The waters sit inside a layered conservation regime — the federal APA Cairuçu (ICMBio) around Paraty's coast and the Juatinga Ecological Reserve (INEA) over the wild peninsula — where anchoring, wake and noise rules make a silent, zero-wake electric fleet a natural regulatory fit for the UNESCO management plan.
signature_routes: Paraty ↔ Saco do Mamanguá (Brazil's only tropical fjord)
Paraty ↔ Vila do Abraão, Ilha Grande (the UNESCO twin-site crossing, ~31 nm)
Paraty ↔ Angra dos Reis (the Costa Verde heritage corridor, ~28 nm)
Paraty bay circuit: Ilha dos Cocos – Lagoa Azul – Praia da Lula – Praia Vermelha (the schooner classic, foiled)

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates electric foiling as the backbone of island and resort mobility at national scale — the playbook for turning an existing boat-borne visitor economy into a clean scheduled network.
